# Development screen for lossless offline catalogue updates

The receiver holds a base snapshot of an artwork catalogue. The server must send an update sufficient to reconstruct the next snapshot's canonical table of string values, row identities and field order exactly. This measures transfer bytes rather than the citation-alert workload. Serialize rows in lexical primary-key order and use identical UTF-8 JSON lines for all methods. All encoders see the complete base and target. The receiver has the base, schema and decoder program. Any data-dependent choice must be included in the transmitted bytes. Count framing, inserted rows, removals, rule exceptions and fallback modes. The canonicalization omits incidental CSV quoting and source row order. A future raw-file transport claim would require a separate benchmark.

Use January–June and June–October 2014 Tate releases for development only. These intervals were already studied for content changes. Test a column patch that describes repeated old→new replacements and explicitly encodes exceptions. For each column compare sparse assignments, grouped new values, and old-value-wide edits followed by exceptions; transmit the shorter representation with its decoder tag. Include both an independently implemented row-level diff and the identical column patch without replacement rules. Also compare whole-target zstd and zstd with the base as a reference, and xdelta3 VCDIFF, all round-tripped with their own decoders. Use the same zstd compression level 19 for the JSON formats. Give general codecs their high-compression setting. Report bytes per interval and end-to-end decoding verification. This first screen requires 5% smaller patches than every control in BOTH intervals to warrant spending untouched external snapshots on the hypothesis. Fixed percentage expresses a bandwidth budget; this two-interval screen cannot qualify a paper. Best available delta encoders, prior art on transformation-based deltas, release sampling and independent publisher holdouts must be settled before any positive paper claim.
